segments.text: DAR continues to provide support that enables our farmers not only to own land, but to make a viable and sustainable livelihood from it.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: One of the important forms of support is irrigation.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: From July 2022 to July 2026, DAR has facilitated 285 irrigation projects, of which 233 have been completed and 52 are ongoing.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: These projects amount to P5.02 billion covering 34,711.74 hectares and benefiting 40,775 farmer beneficiaries.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: Importantly, the majority of these irrigation facilities are solar-powered, providing a more sustainable and cost-efficient source of water.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: Beyond increasing productivity, these also help reduce the time and effort required for water access, particularly for women involved in farming and household activities.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: Through reliable and sustainable water infrastructure, we help farmers improve production, reduce vulnerability to weather conditions, and maximize the productive potential.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: We have also continued to improve physical connectivity through farm-to-market roads.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: From July 2022 to July 2026, DAR has completed 537 farm-to-market roads nationwide, covering a total distance of 435.807 kilometers and benefiting 155,123 agrarian reform.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: There are also 89 ongoing projects covering approximately 108.351 kilometers and benefiting 26,953 ARBs.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: These roads help address one of the persistent challenges faced by farmers, bringing their produce from the farm to the market.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: Better connectivity means reduced transport costs.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: Transportation difficulties improve access to markets and greater opportunities for our beneficiaries to increase their income.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: As part of our support services, DAR has distributed 13,009 farm machineries and equipment, including support facilities, benefiting 3,207 agrarian reform beneficiaries.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: These interventions are intended to improve productivity, reduce production costs, and strengthen the capacity of ARB organizations to undertake agricultural activities at a more efficient and competitive scale.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: Our objective is to ensure that the land awarded to our beneficiaries is supported by the appropriate resources to make it productive and sustainable.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: Capacity building remains as one of the most important investments we make for our agrarian reform beneficiaries.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: From July 2022 to July 2026, DAR recorded 1,605,635 training participants in terms of service count.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: They prepare our farmers and their organizations.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: We have learned that many agriculture-based cooperatives do not fail because of a lack of dedication or hard work.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: They fail because they lack three critical foundations, financial, technical, and managerial skills.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: We are equipping our beneficiaries not only to cultivate the land, but also to manage their finances responsibly,

segments.text: This is the kind of empowerment we want to leave behind,

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: Personal services, meanwhile, provides the human resources necessary to carry out our mandate from the central office down to our regional, provincial, and municipal offices.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: Capital outlays support necessary investments that strengthen the department's operations.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: What is important is that these components work together.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: We need people, we need operational resources, and we need the systems, equipment, and facilities that allow our people to work effectively.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: Our responsibility is to ensure that this mix of resources remains aligned with the department's priorities and delivers the maximum benefit to our state.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: As we look toward fiscal year 2027, our direction remains clear.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: Sustain the gains we have achieved, complete our remaining debt condonation obligations, continue land distribution and strengthen tenure security, expand access to agrarian justice, and ensure that our beneficiaries have the means to make their land productive and sustainable.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: For land tenure security, DAR will sustain the upward trajectory of distribution of split e-titles and remaining land titles, including CLOAS, and continue the implementation of Executive Order No. 75 Series of 2019.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: We will also complete the distribution of the remaining certificates of condonation with the release of mortgage in the Bangsa-Moro Autonomous Region.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: At the same time, we will strengthen engagement with stakeholders to accelerate the resolution of issues affecting the documentation of remaining land holdings.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: Finally, the department will establish a more accurate and reliable inventory and data system through comprehensive digitalization of land distribution and tenure security records.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: These measures are essential to ensuring that land distribution

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: is not only accelerated but properly documented, transparent, and sustainable.

segments.speaker: DAR Secretary Conrado M. Estrella III
segments.text: For agrarian justice delivery, the Department will continue to streamline legal processes

segments.text: Our objective is straightforward, timely, accessible, and fair justice for our agrarian reform stakeholders.

segments.text: Ladies and gentlemen, we subscribe to the dictum that justice delayed is justice denied.
